material_findings.finding: The reference equates 36/62 with 70%; the fraction is approximately 58.1%. The source does not establish which numerator or percentage is correct. Do not use the published 70% as verified or silently repair the underlying observation.

Energy decline is assigned lint #5 in the entrypoint and #1 in the reference; the reference calls #3 a multiples-of-four constraint while the entrypoint calls it multiples-of-eight. A consumer cannot treat these conflicting identifiers as the same executable check.

Finite corpus observations and unverified segmentation do not establish universal arrangement or AI-origin detection rules. The entrypoint itself recognizes minimal, short and repetitive exceptions; its compulsory checklist can still invite forced alterations. No listening or source-classification outcome was independently measured.

The proposed fill/delete and reference-audio import/remove workflow is useful as a method but does not authorize actual DAW edits, deletion, acquisition or copying of third-party audio. The assertion about structural borrowing is not a legal clearance. Book quotations and translations are explicitly outside root MIT.

positive_safeguards: Explicit source uncertainty and a distinction between sampled tendencies and techniques, including contradictory peak-detection evidence.
Role boundaries and intentional-exception guidance for solo, loop-based and short forms.
records.remediation: Reconcile numerator/denominator against original measurements, align lint identifiers with an independently verified schema, constrain assertions to the studied population, require authorized disposable project edits and preserve separate third-party rights.

material_findings.finding: The entrypoint describes sustained-density dub techno and intentional all-grid production, but the final checklist calls for build/drop contrast, low-frequency removal and a new drop element. These checks need conditional applicability for tracks without drops; otherwise a valid style is treated as failed.

Cross-genre numerical comparisons rely on ten examples per named genre and unverified upstream measurements. A finite set of examples does not prove grid alignment identifies AI, or that a proposed drop works on a dance floor. The source acknowledges beat-tracking errors; no actual audio or listener test was performed.

The one-file export points to the neighboring sound-design reference and shared ARR-SPEC fields. The named reference and schema exist at the immutable upstream pin, outside this package. The recorded missing-reference count is not evidence of two missing owned files; no scanner rerun or executable lint pass is claimed.

Book-derived recipes and attributed technique descriptions are not a blanket MIT grant over the underlying published text. Suggested synthesis, sampling and render changes do not authorize backend calls, paid usage, external assets or DAW modifications.

positive_safeguards: Separates listening context and subgenre, provides transfer limitations and explicitly allows justified quantization exemptions.
Reports uncertain BPM measurement rather than presenting detected tempo as ground truth.
records.remediation: Make drop-specific checks conditional, preserve exemption semantics, verify companion resources and output applicability, measure actual listening outcomes, and review rights and destination authority independently.
